findings.detail: Review demonstrated that consumed source and sequence identity alone were insufficient and that independently supplied transition reward and boundary flags could diverge from the recorded event. The final implementation binds the complete consumed request and actual applied action to the original proposal, and binds transition reward, terminal, cutoff, validity and recurrent reset to the original task event. Negative tests cover both findings. Native numeric action tolerance remains the existing conformance tolerance; boolean metadata aliases are rejected.

Ordered fitting windows reconstruct complete available prefixes, maintain separate frozen-base and residual state, and do not bridge overridden or missing observations. BC and PPO use the fixed exported specifications. PPO densities refer to the original five-dimensional Normal draw and two Bernoulli draws; actor channels, source hashes, feature and history hashes, invocation and base identity are authenticated. Model, burn-in, loss, optimizer and checkpoint work is reserved before use.

findings.area: physical capture and offline audit integration
findings.detail: The capture path preserves native per-tick receipts, original requested and admitted packets, distinct proposal and dispatch histories, task rewards and termination, original policy values and the actual pre-cancel bootstrap observation. Emergency overrides do not produce invented actor draws or critic values. Synthetic capture-to-artifact-to-audit controls cover non-PPO null bootstrap and PPO emergency cutoff behavior. All six fixed final checkpoint hashes precede every sealed outcome, including authored and idle references.

The external standard-library reader reconstructs every final counter and stage total from the immutable reservation array, verifies the exact pre-audit prefix, and permits only cleanup audit-forward and checkpoint-load reservations in the suffix. Their deltas must equal the independent audit's reported charges. Worker, audit, configuration, declaration and final-result identities remain bound. Capped, failed or incomplete evidence cannot be promoted to completion or qualification. Final worker qualification now requires verified and complete readback together with completed worker status.

The outer clock begins before substantial imports and is passed unchanged to the worker. Worker and external inventory timeouts preserve finalization reserve. BaseException and cleanup failures attempt owned-tree revocation; failed inspection uses direct known-worker revocation without asserting descendant closure. Completion requires a completed worker, verified complete readback, reconciled closed costs, zero owned descendants, confirmed cleanup and publication within the original 1,800 seconds. The terminal receipt and successful process exit remain authoritative after final receipt publication.

Freeze and execution require the complete matching source inventory, clean frozen source revision, exact configuration and budget, pinned host/runtime identity, and distinct accepted review identities with unchanged review bytes. Automatic retry and extension are false. Execution admission happens before model draws, fitting or host acquisition. The independently computed 182-file hash matches this record's source identity.

Software acceptance preserves the original physical qualification, matched reference, owner-feel and morphology boundaries. A successful software review or structurally verified partial artifact is not a trained-skill acceptance. Audit reconstruction authenticates recorded fitting and retained checkpoints without repeating optimization, and does not establish a new inference-latency measurement.
